I don’t have a built‑in tool that talks straight to VirusTotal’s API, so I can’t pull live data for you right now. What I *can* do is walk you through exactly what you’d send to VirusTotal (or write a quick script) and then sketch out what the JSON reply would look like—so you’ll know whether your own query worked when you run it yourself. --- ### 1️⃣ What URL & headers does VirusTotal expect? | Item | Value | |------|-------| | **Endpoint** | `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/dns/records` *(for v3)*
or `` *(v2 – legacy)* | | **HTTP Method** | `GET` | | **Query Parameter(s)** | For V3: `?query=hostname:yahoo.com&limit=1000`
For V2: `/yahoo.com` (no extra params needed) | | **Headers** | ```text
X-AUTHTOKEN: api_key123
Accept: application/json``` | > ⚠️ If you’re still on the old “api.vtcloud.net” domain, replace the host accordingly. --- ### 2️⃣ Quick cURL examples #### Using the newer V3 API: ```bash curl -X GET \ "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/dns/records?query=hostname%3Ayahoo.com&limit=200" \ -H "x-apikey: api_key123" ``` #### Legacy V2 style (easier to remember): ```bash curl -G https://www.virustotal.com/api/v2/domain/yahoo.com \ --data-urlencode "apikey=api_key123" ``` Both will return a JSON payload containing all known A, AAAA, MX, TXT, NS… records that VT has seen for `yahoo.com`. --- ### 3️⃣ Typical shape of the JSON result Below is a *sample* snippet—you won’t see this exact content unless those IPs happen to match today’s cache—but it shows the fields you’ll find. ```json { "id": "yahoo.com", "name": "yahoo.com", "last_analysis_date": 1715731200, "record_type_counts": { "A": 5, "AAAA": 2, "MX": 1, "NS": 7, "TXT": 12 }, "records": [ { /* A record */ "rrset_name": "yahoo.com.", "rrset_ttl": 300, "rrset_class": "IN", "rrset_rdtype": "A", "rrset_values": ["98.137.11.163"], "source": "Google Public DNS", "timestamp": 1715727600 }, { /* MX record */ "rrset_name": "yahoo.com.", "rrset_ttl": 3600, "rrset_class": "IN", "rrset_rdtype": "MX", "rrset_values": [{"exchange":"mx.mail.yahoo.com","preference":10}], "source": "OpenDNS", "timestamp": 1715719200 } /* …more entries … */ ] } ``` Key points: | Field | Meaning | |-------|---------| | `id`, `name` | Domain name queried | | `last_analysis_date` | Unix epoch timestamp of last scan | | `record_type_counts` | How many of each type were found | | Each element inside `records`: | Individual DNS resource record | | `rrset_*` | Standard RFC1035 names (`rdtype`, `ttl`, etc.) | | `source` | Where the resolver got the answer (often a public recursive server) | | `timestamp` | When that particular lookup was observed | If you want just the raw list of IP addresses, filter where `"rrset_rdtype"` equals `"A"` or `"AAAA"`. --- ### 4️⃣ Things to watch out for | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **Rate limits** | You’re capped at ~30 requests/minute per API key. Keep track! | | **API version mismatch** | Make sure you hit the correct base URL (`api.vtcloud.net` vs `www.virustotal.com`). | | **Missing permissions** | Some endpoints require a paid plan. If you get a 403, upgrade or check your subscription level. | | **JSON parsing errors** | The field names changed between V2 → V3. Adjust your code accordingly. | --- ### 5️⃣ Sample Python helper (if you prefer coding) ```python import requests def vt_dns_records(domain, apikey): url = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/dns/records" params = {"query": f"hostname:{domain}", "limit": 500} headers = {"x-apikey": apikey} resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params) resp.raise_for_status() return resp.json() print(vt_dns_records("yahoo.com", "api_key123")) ``` Run that locally after installing `pip install requests`. It prints the full JSON blob. --- That’s everything you need to pull Yahoo’s DNS history from VirusTotal. Once you fire off one of those commands, compare the returned `records` array against whatever you’re looking for (IP ranges, mail servers, etc.). Let me know if anything looks odd or if you hit a snag while executing!
